In the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma game-hosting platform), a customer on a Don't Starve Together (DST family) game server filed a support ticket titled "i can't delete my world" saying "how do i delete my world if you can deleted can you do it?" (garbled, likely means "if I can't delete it myself, can you do it for me?").

I need to understand:
1. Does the platform have any customer-facing feature to delete/reset a DST world's save data? Check components/customer/ for DST-specific settings/world-management UI, the File Manager (they might be expected to delete world folders via SFTP file browser instead), and lib/game-config.ts's DST schema for any "reset world" style action or field.
2. If there's no dedicated "delete world" button, is deleting via the File Manager actually possible for a DST server — i.e., can a customer browse to and delete the world save directory via the existing file browser (app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts or the hosting one at app/api/hosting/files)? Check whether DST servers even get File Manager access (some families might not expose SFTP/file browsing at all — check server detail page tabs for which families show a Files tab).
3. Is there a known reason a customer might NOT be able to delete a file/folder via File Manager — e.g., a permissions issue, the world files being owned by a different UID inside the container (root vs a game user), the DST server process holding a lock on save files while running, or a path-traversal/validation guard in the delete-file action that might incorrectly reject a legitimate world folder name?
4. Check lib/game-config.ts's DST schema and any DST-specific worker code (search worker/ for "dst" or "yeetzone" — I recall from a previous incident this session that DST uses the yeetzone image and needs a TOKEN) for any relevant detail about where DST world saves actually live on disk (which directory), since that tells us what the customer would need to delete.

Report concisely under 400 words with file:line citations. This is investigation only — do not modify code or touch any customer server.

content.text: Good — confirmed unconditional (no per-family gate visible; passed straight into the tab renderer for every family). That's enough for the report.

No per-family exclusion of the Files tab — it's rendered the same for every family, DST included.

## Findings

**1. No dedicated "delete/reset world" feature.** `lib/game-config.ts`'s `DST` schema (lines 952-972) has only `NAME`, `MAX_PLAYERS`, `PASSWORD`, `TOKEN` fields — no reset/wipe action. `components/customer/` has no DST-specific world-management component; `GameSettings.tsx` etc. are generic and driven purely by this schema. There is no customer-facing "delete world" button anywhere.

**2. Deleting via File Manager is possible and not family-gated.** `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:562-575` renders `FileManager` for any server (any family) when `status === "RUNNING"`; there's no per-family exclusion (confirmed — `gameFamily` is passed through only for cosmetic labeling, not to hide the Files tab). `FileManager.tsx` calls server actions in `lib/actions-files.ts` (`listFiles`, `deleteEntry`, etc., imported at `components/customer/FileManager.tsx:4-12`), which delete via `lib/sftp.ts:448-465` (`removePath` → `client.rmdir(path, true)` for directories or `client.delete(path)` for files). The customer would need to browse to and delete the DST data directory themselves.

**3. No permission/lock bug found in the delete path.** `withSftp` (`lib/sftp.ts:161-189`) always connects as `root` using the server's root password (`username: "root"`, line 178), so container-internal UID mismatches (DST/yeetzone container writing as a non-root game user) are irrelevant — host-root SFTP can delete regardless of in-container ownership. Path validation (`normalizePath`/`validateName`, `lib/sftp.ts:80-106`) only rejects `..`, NUL bytes, overlong names, and non-absolute paths — a legitimate path like `/opt/dst/...` would not be rejected. Linux filesystem semantics also mean an open save file being written by the running DST process does not block `unlink`/`rmdir`. So there's no code-level bug blocking deletion; the customer's real obstacle is almost certainly just not knowing the path or not having/using SFTP-equivalent File Manager access, or being unaware the "Files" tab exists.

**4. World save location.** DST is provisioned via `-v /opt/dst:/data yeetzone/dontstarvetogether:latest` (`prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts:86`; confirmed again in `test/game-variant.test.ts:49`), and `lib/game-control.ts:279` lists `dataRoots: ["/opt/dst"]`. So on the host, `/opt/dst` (mounted to `/data` in-container) is where the customer's cluster/world lives — deleting the cluster subfolder under `/opt/dst` via File Manager (server must be `RUNNING` first, per line 564) is the closest thing to "delete my world" today. Exact internal subpath (e.g. `Cluster_1/Master/save`) isn't hardcoded anywhere in this repo — only referenced generically in a blog post (`prisma/seed-blog-wave3-wave4-games.ts:668`, mentioning `cluster.ini`/`worldgenoverride.lua`), so support would need to tell the customer to browse into `/opt/dst` and identify the cluster folder by name/date rather than a known fixed path.

**Bottom line for the ticket:** there's no self-service "reset world" button; the customer can delete world data themselves via the account's File Manager (Files tab, server must be running) by navigating to `/opt/dst` and removing the cluster folder, or support can do it for them over the same path — no known code bug prevents either.
